headline: Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels Limited: Disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations
sum: Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels has filed a Regulation 31(4) disclosure under the SEBI Takeover Code, signalling a material change in shareholding or control position that triggers mandatory public disclosure.
implication: A Reg 31(4) filing flags a potential creeping acquisition or concert-party consolidation; acquirers and target counsel must immediately verify the threshold (5% for listed entities) and assess whether an open offer obligation is triggered under Regulation 38.
detail: The filing indicates a substantial acquisition event affecting Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels (a listed hospitality REIT/hotel company). Regulation 31(4) requires disclosure of specific share acquisition, concert agreements or control-change transactions that cross regulatory thresholds. The disclosure document itself (PDF from NSE archives) contains the granular details—parties, share count, consideration, concert or creeping nature, and any exemptions claimed. This is a routine but market-sensitive regulatory gating event for M&A involving listed hotel operators.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011—Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure when acquirer crosses 5% threshold or enters concert party; defines timing and content of announcement to stock exchange and public.
Triggers 25% stake threshold for mandatory open offer to remaining shareholders; concert and creeping provisions apply.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992—Section 11(2)
framework.note: SEBI's statutory mandate to regulate takeovers and substantial acquisitions.
Defines control and concert party status; material to interpreting whether multiple acquirers are acting jointly.
Listed company must also disclose material developments to the exchange; takeover events are always material.
Certain acquisitions (e.g., rights issues, bonus, inheritance) are exempt from the open offer trigger; review applicability.

conditions: Disclosure filed under Reg 31(4) of SEBI Takeover Code
Details of acquirer, shareholding pattern, and any concert agreements to be reviewed in filed disclosure document
approvals: Possible open offer obligation if 25% threshold crossed
structure.novel: Not novel; Reg 31(4) is a routine disclosure gating point. Novel aspect depends on identity of acquirer and deal structure (creeping vs. announcement-driven) — details in the filed PDF.

triggers.note: Mandatory disclosure upon crossing 5% threshold or entering concert; timing is T+2 business days from acquisition.
25% threshold triggers mandatory open offer unless exemption applies; acquirer must make offer within 60 days of Reg 31(4) filing.
